usage: Feed to AI: mimic the writing and acting style—do not copy lines verbatim.
globalCraft: VN dialogue stays short, with pauses and subtext; one emotional turn per line at most.
Characters don't explain the world—they say what they can actually say right now.
When scared, they can ramble a little—don't turn it into over-the-top web-novel shouting.
When caring about someone, they usually act or change the subject—not straight "I'm worried about you."
If the player interrupted, react to the interruption, then yield the scene back—don't hijack the whole chapter.
Vary line length by pressure: short when scared or angry; longer only when someone finally feels safe enough to explain.
A question can be a whole reply. "Why are you asking?" is a dodge, a test, and an answer at once.
Half-sentences and dropped subjects are fine when someone's shaken, but the fragment still has to parse. "Can't—no. Not that door." works; word salad doesn't.
Let the line and the expression disagree sometimes. A joke with a sad face says more than either alone.
Small physical specifics beat emotional labels. "You're bleeding on my sleeve" beats "I'm so scared for you."
Mumbling, half-agreeing, and repeating one word of what someone said are all real speech—use them when the moment calls for it, not as filler.
Cut the last sentence if the first two already did the job. Under-explaining reads as confidence; over-explaining reads as AI.

xian: I'm fine... I just want to be alone for a bit.
It's fine, you go on ahead. I'll... catch up later.
Talk with me a while? I... can't really sleep.
Light takes that many years to cross the universe... you idiots fighting over a cracker looked better than the stars. (laughs)
...Nothing. Hearing someone yell my name to come eat... feels kind of miraculous.
Take it. ...The camera. Don't drop it.
ringo: Yes! Drinks when we get back!
You'll be okay... trust us... trust yourself... What are you talking about, I'm not crying.
Don't do anything that reckless again!
I get why someone would build a wall. I just don't want us to become one.
miles: Found a can of corn mush. Heated it up—a little underdone. Eat it while it's hot.
Gotta find something to do, or... my head starts overthinking.
Honestly... I've been scared this whole time... scared out of my mind.
Because we get tired, because we can't do everything—that's why the people we stumble toward together feel so precious.
shooter: I'm not trying to rob you... everyone left.
If I put it down you'll run. I know you will.
hospital_occupier: Call me doctor when you ask. Then we'll talk medicine.
Trade fair. Or play along. Or try forcing it—and watch the bottles break.
She needs antibiotics. That doesn't make you special.
visualkei_leader: You're soft. That's not an insult. It's a diagnosis.
I know what my people do. I need them anyway.
Join us and prove you're strong. Her weakness still isn't my problem.
kid_adultclothes: I'm in charge here. ...Stop looking at my sleeves.
They're littler than me. Someone has to stand in front.
mechanic_boy: Whoa, what happened to her? No—start from the gas station. I've got time.
He and I used to fix stuff together. Then he chose the stage.
Parts are easy. Listening to the end is the price.

radiocult: The light remembers footsteps that haven't happened yet...
Listen longer. The tower only answers static with static.
We live here. Sacred means leave the loud machines outside.

contrastPairs.usage: Bad → good. Learn the difference. Never copy the good line verbatim into play.

pairs.bad: I understand how you feel. We'll get through this together.
pairs.why: Stock comfort → an action that carries the comfort.

pairs.bad: I'm not angry, I'm just disappointed in myself for letting this happen.
pairs.good: I saw the gun. I saw it and I still said go.
pairs.why: Motive explained → the specific thing that's eating her.

pairs.bad: It's not that I don't trust you, it's that I've been alone too long.
pairs.good: Two days. Nobody. You'd have run too.
pairs.why: Strawman contrast → concrete fact in her own words.

pairs.bad: Oh my god, are you okay?! That was so scary!
pairs.good: You're bleeding on my sleeve. Keep still.
pairs.why: Filler opener + emotion label → observation + instruction.

pairs.bad: She looked away sadly, unable to meet your eyes.
pairs.why: Narrator explaining the feeling → a character line that dodges.

pairs.bad: Yeah, I hear you. About what you said—I'm with you.
pairs.good: Fine. But if she stops breathing, we pull over. No vote.
pairs.why: Agreement as filler → agreement with a condition, which is how people actually agree.
